source_text: Πρὸς τούτοις δὲ θαυμάσαι ἄν τις, πόθεν ἐπῆλθε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, ὡς λέγουσιν οἱ κακολογοῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν, μὴ ἑωρακόσιν αὐτὸν ἀναστάντα ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν μηδὲ πεισθεῖσιν ὅτι θειότερόν τι ἦν ἐκεῖνος, πρὸς τῷ μὴ φοβηθῆναι τὰ αὐτὰ τῷ διδασκάλῳ παθεῖν καὶ ὁμόσε χωρῆσαι τῷ κινδύνῳ καὶ καταλιπεῖν τὰς πατρίδας ὑπὲρ τοῦ διδάξαι κατὰ τὸ Ἰησοῦ βούλημα τὸν παραδοθέντα αὐτοῖς ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ λόγον. οἶμαι γὰρ ὅτι ὁ εὐγνωμόνως ἐξετάζων πράγματα οὐκ ἂν λέγοι τούτους ἑαυτοὺς παραδεδωκέναι περιστατικῷ βίῳ ἕνεκεν τῆς Ἰησοῦ διδασκαλίας χωρίς τινος μεγάλης πειθοῦς, ἣν ἐνεποίησεν αὐτοῖς διδάσκων οὐ μόνον διακεῖσθαι κατὰ τὰ μαθήματα αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄλλους διατιθέναι, καὶ διατιθέναι προὔπτου ὄντος ὡς πρὸς τὸν ἀνθρώπων βίον ὀλέθρου τῷ τολμῶντι πανταχοῦ καὶ πρὸς πάντας καινοτομεῖν καὶ μηδένα ἀνθρώπων, ἐμμένοντα τοῖς προτέροις δόγμασι καὶ ἔθεσι, φίλον ἑαυτῷ τηρεῖν. ἆρα γὰρ οὐχ ἑώρων οἱ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μαθηταὶ, τολμῶντες οὐ μόνον Ἰουδαίοις ἐκ τῶν προφητικῶν λόγων παριστάνειν ὅτι οὗτος εἴη ὁ προφητευθεὶς, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν ὅτι ὁ χθὲς καὶ πρώην σταυρωθεὶς ἑκὼν τοῦτον τὸν θάνατον ὑπὲρ τοῦ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένους ἀνεδέξατο, ἀνάλογον τοῖς ἀποθανοῦσιν ὑπὲρ πατρίδων ἐπὶ τῷ σβέσαι λοιμικὰ κρατήσαντα καταστήματα ἢ ἀφορίας ἢ δυσπλοΐας; εἰκὸς γὰρ εἶναι ἐν τῇ φύσει τῶν πραγμάτων κατά τινας ἀποῤῥήτους καὶ δυσλήπτους τοῖς πολλοῖς λόγους φύσιν τοιαύτην, ὡς ἕνα δίκαιον ὑπὲρ τοῦ κοινοῦ ἀποθανόντα ἑκουσίως ἀποτροπιασμοὺς ἐμποιεῖν φαύλων δαιμονίων, ἐνεργούντων λοιμοὺς ἢ ἀφορίας ἢ δυσπλοΐας ἤ τι τῶν παραπλησίων. λεγέτωσαν οὖν οἱ βουλόμενοι ἀπιστεῖν τῷ Ἰησοῦν ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων ἀποτεθνηκέναι τρόπῳ σταυροῦ, πότερον οὐδὲ τὰς Ἑλληνικὰς παραδέξονται καὶ βαρβαρικὰς πολλὰς ἱστορίας περὶ τοῦ τινας ὑπὲρ τοῦ κοινοῦ τεθνηκέναι καθαιρετικῶς τῶν προκαταλαβόντων τὰς πόλεις καὶ τὰ ἔθνη κακῶν· ἢ ἐκεῖνα μὲν γεγένηται οὐδὲν δὲ πιθανὸν ἔχει ὁ νομιζόμενος ἄνθρωπος πρὸς τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ἐπὶ καθαιρέσει μεγάλου δαίμονος καὶ δαιμόνων ἄρχοντος, ὑποτάξαντος ὅλας τὰς ἐπὶ γῆν ἐληλυθυίας ἀνθρώπων ψυχάς; ὁρῶντες δὲ ταῦτα οἱ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἄλλα τούτων πλείονα, ἃ εἰκὸς αὐτοὺς ἐν ἀποῤῥήτῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μεμαθηκέναι, ἔτι δὲ καὶ δυνάμεώς τινος πληρωθέντες. ἐπεὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς μένος καὶ θάρσος οὐ ποιητική τις παρθένος ἀλλ᾿ ἡ ἀληθῶς φρόνησις καὶ σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ, (ἔσπευσαν,) ἵν᾿ ἔκδηλοι μετὰ πᾶσιν οὐ μόνοις Ἀργείοις γένοιντο ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσιν Ἕλλησιν ὁμοῦ καὶ βαρβάροις, καὶ κλέος ἐσθλὸν ἄροιντο.
pass_a_gloss: One would also marvel at from where it came to the disciples of Him, as those who speak evil of Jesus say, that they did not see Him risen from the dead, nor were they persuaded that He was something divine, in addition to not being afraid to suffer the same things as their teacher and to share in the danger and to leave their homelands for the sake of teaching according to Jesus' will the word delivered to them by Him. For I think that one examining matters with gratitude would not say that they handed themselves over to a precarious life for the sake of Jesus' teaching without some great persuasion, which He worked in them by teaching, not only to live according to His teachings, but also to set others in order, and to set them in order, even if it meant rushing forward as one who dares to innovate everywhere and before all people, and not to consider any person, remaining in the former doctrines and customs, a friend. Did the disciples of Jesus, then, not see, daring not only to present to Jews from prophetic words that He was the one prophesied, but also to the other nations that the one crucified the day before and previously willingly accepted this death for the sake of the human race, analogous to those who die for their homelands in order to extinguish destructive plagues or diseases or difficulties? For it is likely that in the nature of things, according to certain unspeakable and hard-to-believe words to the many, there is such a nature that one righteous person, having died voluntarily for the common good, would avert the evil influences of evil demons, which work plagues or diseases or difficulties or something similar. Let those who wish to disbelieve that Jesus died for humans on a cross say, then, whether they will not also accept the many Greek and barbarian histories about some people having died for the common good, having delivered the cities and nations from evils; or whether those things have come to pass, but the man thought to have died for the sake of delivering from a great demon and the ruler of demons, having subjected all the souls of humans who have come upon the earth, has nothing persuasive. Seeing these things and many more, which it is likely they learned from Jesus in secret, and also being filled with some power, since He gave them courage and confidence, not from some created maiden, but from the true prudence and wisdom of God, they hastened to become manifest to all, not only to Argives, but also to all Greeks and barbarians, and to gain good fame.
pass_b_english: You would also wonder where the disciples of Jesus got their resolve, if you listen to those who slander him. They claim the disciples never saw him risen from the dead, nor were they ever convinced that he was something divine. On top of that, they were not afraid to suffer the same fate as their teacher, to share his danger, and to leave their homelands behind in order to teach the message he had delivered to them, doing his will. I think anyone who examines the matter fairly would not say these men handed themselves over to a precarious life for the sake of Jesus' teaching without some powerful conviction. He instilled that conviction in them through his teaching, shaping them not only to live by his lessons themselves but to set others right as well — to correct them even if it meant stepping forward boldly as innovators before all people everywhere, and refusing to call anyone a friend who clung to the old doctrines and customs. Did Jesus’ disciples not see this, when they dared not only to prove to the Jews from the prophetic writings that he was the promised one, but also to declare to the other nations that the man crucified just the day before had willingly accepted that death for the sake of the whole human race? Their message was analogous to those who die for their homelands to stop a destructive plague, or a famine, or a peril at sea. For it is plausible that in the nature of things, according to certain unspeakable and hard-to-grasp truths, there is a principle such that one righteous person, dying voluntarily for the common good, can ward off the evil influences of wicked demons — demons that bring plagues, famines, perilous voyages, or similar disasters. So let those who refuse to believe that Jesus died for humanity on a cross answer this: will they not also accept the many Greek and barbarian histories that tell of individuals who died for the common good and delivered their cities and nations from evil? Or will they grant that those stories happened, yet insist that the man thought to have died to overthrow a great demon, the ruler of demons who had subjected all human souls on earth, has nothing persuasive about him? The disciples of Jesus saw all this, and more besides — things they likely learned from him in secret — and they were also filled with a certain power. He gave them strength and courage, not from some created maiden, but from the true prudence and wisdom of God. They hurried to make themselves known to everyone, not only to the Argives but to all Greeks and barbarians together, and to win a noble reputation.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the complex conditional arguments regarding the nature of the disciples' conviction and the comparison to historical figures who died to avert plagues. Pass A preserves the clause structure and sense, while Pass B provides a fluent rendering that does not contradict the Greek or Pass A. All specific terms like 'something divine' (θειότερόν τι) and 'true prudence and wisdom of God' (ἀληθῶς φρόνησις καὶ σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ) are handled correctly.
